Indigenous Health Assessment (Adults 15–54 Years)

Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • Recurrent episodes (1–2 ×/day) over the past 6–8 weeks of right-hand pins-and-needles, transient right arm and leg weakness, and temporary abnormal gait  
  • Associated fatigue, episodic nausea, difficulty holding coffee cup, transient “something in throat” sensation during episodes  
  • Family history of stroke; patient self-initiated daily low-dose aspirin
- Relevant family medical history:
  • Father: carotid artery surgery to reduce stroke risk (implies cerebrovascular disease)
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  • Aspirin 75 mg orally once daily – self-prescribed
  • No other regular medicines reported
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded
- Sexual and reproductive health: Lives with wife; no other details recorded
- Physical activity and nutrition: Not recorded
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:
  • Tobacco: Non-smoker  
  • Alcohol and other substances: Not recorded
- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): Not recorded
- Vision problems or recent changes:
  • Wears glasses; no new visual disturbance reported during episodes
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:
  • Lives with wife  
  • Employed as a medical doctor (plastic surgery)

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference: Not recorded
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums): Not recorded
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed): Not recorded
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen): Not recorded
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria): Not recorded

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed): Previous cholesterol and diabetes screen reportedly normal (date/results not documented)
- Cervical screening, STI screen, mammogram, other pathology: Not applicable / Not recorded
- Other: Urgent referral to TIA (Transient Ischemic Attack) clinic arranged for carotid Doppler, brain imaging, and stroke risk work-up

Management Plan

- Urgent referral sent today to local TIA clinic; patient advised clinic should contact him within 1–2 days (before weekend)
- Provided TIA clinic and PALS contact numbers; instructed to phone clinic this afternoon or next morning to confirm appointment
- Safety-net advice: If symptoms recur and are prolonged, attend Emergency Department immediately; otherwise, contact GP service for further guidance
- Discussed provisional diagnosis of TIA; emphasized urgency despite patient’s young age
- Advised to monitor symptoms closely; no documented change to current aspirin use
- Follow-up: Await TIA clinic assessment; patient to re-contact GP if any delays or deterioration

Quality checks

● Missing but clinically expected elements: BP, pulse, BMI, waist circumference, detailed alcohol intake, diet/exercise assessment, immunisation review, mental health screening, hearing assessment, urinalysis, full medication reconciliation.  
● Internal contradictions: Initial mention of “problems with asthma” by clinician was not explored further (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Occasional audio/video drop-outs but core clinical information understandable; some minor gaps in detail.
